source: Changes to the feature values built from PanPhon and Hayes, each with the source that decides it. A value marked 'derived' follows a convention of the cited table, applied to a segment the table does not list.

overrides.source: Hayes (2009), Introductory Phonology, feature tables of ch. 4, as converted to CSV by Gorman (github.com/kylebgorman/hayes2009, dataprep/Features.csv)
overrides.reason: Hayes gives the alveolar approximant no tongue-body value; PanPhon's [+high] describes the English bunched r, not the symbol.

overrides.source: Hayes (2009), Introductory Phonology, feature tables of ch. 4, as converted to CSV by Gorman (github.com/kylebgorman/hayes2009, dataprep/Features.csv)
overrides.reason: Hayes gives [ɹ] [-round]; the IPA chart symbol carries no lip rounding.
[ɐ] is the near-open central vowel; PHOIBLE gives it [+low, -front, -back], like Hayes's near-open [æ] [+low].
Hayes does not list [ɐ]; PHOIBLE gives the near-open central vowel [-front, -back].
Hayes does not list [ɜ]; PHOIBLE gives the open-mid central vowel [-front, -back].
[ɜ] is the open-mid central vowel; PHOIBLE gives it [-back]. PanPhon's [+back] makes it identical to the open-mid back [ʌ].
